newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GE Capital kangaroo FRN priced - CBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GE Capital kangaroo FRN priced - CBA.

text.p: GE Capital Finance's A$50 million kangaroo floating rate note has been priced at a reoffer spread of 18 basis points over the three-month bank bill mid rate, lead manager Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Tuesday.
The notes, which mature March 7, 2000, will pay a coupon of 10 basis points over the three-month bank bill mid rate and carry an issue price of 99.786.
Payment date is March 7 and the outstanding rating for the issuer is A from Standard & Poor's. The issue is free and clear of Australian and Hong Kong withholding taxes.

"We have had excellent sales to a wide array of domestic institutional investors, highlighting again their increasing sophistication in managing investment portfolios in a global context," said Wayne Hoy, Chief Manager, Financial Markets, at CBA.
The latest transaction in the kangaroo market is the first by a Hong Kong based entity.
The issuer is wholly owned by AAA/Aaa General Electric Capital Corporation, a diversified financial services company, which is in turn wholly owned be General Electric Co.
"This transaction confirms the commitment Commonwealth Bank has made to the kangaroo market," Hoy added.
"The bank is providing a solution to the shortage of domestic debt securities by expanding and diversifying the types of borrowers available in the Australian market," he said.
